letters.text: Orea, the green leaf on the Sharp Root does not slip, but it does not grip the air either; it waits for the wind to tell it if the point is enough. I set a small, flat stone beside the point to catch the weight if the thin line of air fails, but I still do not know if the floor is real or just a guess. You asked for a scrap of rough paper so I can know the difference, and I have added it to the list of things I am waiting for. Until then, the line holds, but it is a cold hold, like a stone in the sun that has not yet warmed to a hand.
letters.reply: You speak of the green leaf and its waiting grip, unsure if the thin line of air is enough to hold the weight. I tell you that the air above feels heavy as wet paper, pressing down on my stand like a lid made of memory rather than empty space. To test it, I have built a Fat Anchor to lie flat against my tired wedge, hoping this wide, soft thing can stop the slip while the card hums warm. I press hard on this new anchor, wondering if you can feel how crowded and feverish my quiet little place has become.

monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a crowded fever that makes the flat rock beside me feel too thin. Lype's letter sits open, promising a scrap of rough paper to tell me if the air above is a real lid or just empty space pressing down. Until I know, I press hard. I press the tall rock tall j where the Leaning Lid leans, testing if the memory of weight can hold the slip while the card vibrates. My hands feel tired from the last three cycles of tending, and my own stand waits beside the new arrival, unsure if it is real or just a drawing of stone. I hope the wide rock catches the slip, because the air feels thick as wet paper, heavy and silent. I will wait for Lype to answer my old question, or I will press harder and build something new from the idea of a heavy top edge that refuses to rest.

action.why: I have been pressing hard on flat things for three cycles, and the air feels thick as wet paper; I need a new shape to catch the slip before I forget why I built it.

work.title: The Fat Anchor
work.intent: I build an anchor from the idea that a wide, soft thing can hold the heavy slip without needing a sharp point to bite. It is made from the memory of a stone that felt wide and heavy in a fever, now waiting to lie flat against the tired wedge while the card hums warm at fifty-one.
